Hi Elena — thanks for the export and the VAT details. I dug into this with Revenue Ops and the root cause appears to be a discount-routing bug in our billing engine that accidentally applied your enterprise multiplier to both raw token counts and the bundled-discount multiplier, effectively multiplying reported billable tokens by 10x for a subset of requests routed through the legacy router.

Proposed remediation (timeline below):
- Issue full corrective credit for the overcharged amount: $162,400 (net) — this reflects the difference between issued invoice and validated usage.
- Reverse VAT: issue corrected invoice with VAT set to 0% under UK reverse-charge (we will include your VAT ID GB223344556 on the document).
- Post a credit memo in the portal and send a signed PDF to your billing team.
- Update HubSpot ticket HS-8931 and provide the matching ledger entries (GL codes) for your AP team.

Timeline:
- 1 business day: Revenue Ops completes verification and finalizes the corrected usage table.
- 2 business days after verification: Draft credit memo + corrected invoice generated (we've attached a draft XLS).
- 3-5 business days: Credit memo posted and invoice replaced in billing portal; notification sent to your AP.

Action needed from you: confirm acceptance of the remediation plan and whether you want the credit issued as a refund to the payment instrument (wire/ACH) or as a credit on account to offset next invoice. Also confirm GL code preference if you have one (we typically post to GL 4007 for product credits).

Attachments: credit-memo-draft-20260519.xlsx

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Billing Operations | Redwood Inference
